title: Schema Negotiator: SDK/CLI API version handshake & graceful-adapter for legacy analytics clients
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem statement: Our telemetry pipeline currently requires clients (SDK/CLI/API) to emit a single canonical schema version. With multiple SDK releases and CLI installs in the wild, we are seeing ingestion errors, high rejection rates for older clients, and difficulty in rolling out schema changes that are both backwards- and forwards-compatible. Goal: build a lightweight Schema Negotiator service and client-side handshake that enables: (1) explicit version negotiation between SDK/CLI and the telemetry gateway, (2) automated per-tenant compatibility adapters in the gateway for legacy payloads, (3) a registry of supported schema features and transformation rules, (4) a gradual canary migration path with validation and telemetry-aware sampling so we can monitor quality regressions. The work here focuses on the backend negotiator, gateway adapter hooks, and the SDK handshake spec. The implementation must be incremental (no big-bang switch) and support runtime feature flags for migration rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Negotiator API defined: GET /negotiate and POST /negotiate that returns a canonical schema_version and a list of supported transforms (JSON path rules)
SDK/CLI handshake proposal documented and approved by DX and Security (spec in Confluence), with example client code snippets for JS/Python/Go
Telemetry gateway can apply at least 3 transformation rules to map legacy envelopes to the current schema (prefix rename, field flattening, timestamp normalization)
End-to-end integration test: legacy SDK v1.2 payload sent to gateway and accepted after adapter transform, verified in analytics dataset (QA workspace)
Canary rollout plan created: cohort selection, sampling rate controls, monitoring dashboards (error rate, mapping failure rate, data-quality metrics)
Schema registry entries created for the first two versions and accessible via Negotiator API
Security review completed and threat model updated for Negotatiator endpoints
Migration playbook & rollback steps documented and linked from ticket

notes: Design tradeoffs: We chose an HTTP-based negotiation over embedding version headers into every event to allow future richer metadata (capabilities, max_payload_size).
Performance consideration: Negotiator responses will be cached at gateway per-token for 5m to avoid extra RTT on hot clients. We will measure cache hit rate and tweak TTLs during canary.
Observability: Create per-version metrics (ingested_count, transform_failures, downstream_schema_mismatch) and add to console-telemetry dashboards.

Backward compatibility: Adapter transforms should be idempotent and logged with small payload samples for debugging. Keep transformation rules declarative to allow non-dev ops to adjust mappings via UI later.

Fallback behaviour: If negotiation fails, gateway should attempt best-effort auto-detect (heuristic field matching) and route to a quarantine topic for manual inspection rather than rejecting outright.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-2): Spec finalization, Negotiator API skeleton, in-memory schema registry, unit tests for transforms
Phase 2 (week 3): Gateway adapter integration, cache layer, auth scopes & rate-limiting hooks
Phase 3 (week 4): SDK/CLI handshake PRs for JS/Python/Go, add client-side deprecation warnings
Phase 4 (week 5): Canary rollout to 5% of traffic for a subset of tenants, monitor metrics and validate datasets
Phase 5 (week 6): Iterate transforms, expand canary, begin deprecation notices and documentation for customer upgrade paths
